design_candidates.name: Family-member positives with a many-positive objective
design_candidates.change: In the generator, define each synthetic family as a parameter distribution (shape family, count, thickness, scale, noise level, phase, placement) and emit a family id with every render; draw the two views of a pair as two INDEPENDENT members of the same family, never two renders of one program. In matching_loss_v2 replace the in-batch index targets of the global InfoNCE with family labels (SupCon: all same-family items in the batch are positives) or, equivalently, a cross-entropy head over thousands of family ids on the pooled coarse features; drop the 5x variance and 1x covariance terms; keep the mask loss only if the family has a defined mask; keep the local Sinkhorn term only with family-level targets. Positive views keep time shift, time/frequency masking and band gain only (see candidate 2).
design_candidates.mechanism: Two renders of one program share exact geometry, so a few easy shared bits solve the pair and suppress learning of the texture, blob and streak statistics that spectrogram types are made of; this suppression happens under contrastive but not supervised loss (Chen and Li). Positives drawn from other instances raised transfer and cut augmentation dependence (NNCLR), SupCon features transfer best to cross-domain few-shot (62.79 vs 60.01 CE vs 61.23 self-sup), supervised embeddings beat MoCo-style ones for one-shot transfer (Tian et al.), and VICReg-style terms are the most augmentation-sensitive family on a small CNN from scratch. Removing the shortcut is the single change that addresses the diagnosed loss of glitch information in epoch 1; it is the v15 scope review's own conclusion.
design_candidates.data_budget_change: none (synthetic data only; one labeled reference at enrollment; the 600-image unlabeled standardization set already declared)
design_candidates.expected_effect: Predicted to stop the epoch-1 destruction: trained fine/middle/coarse blocks should no longer fall below the same blocks at random on DEV (current -0.121 / -0.199 / -0.258 AP). Beating random is not predicted by any published number; a tie with random on DEV would already be a positive result relative to v0.1-v0.3. Pre-register against the multi-seed random control and the fusion bar.
design_candidates.cost: Moderate. Generator change: a family-id and resampling path, about a day of work. Loss change: tens of lines. Training cost unchanged from v0.14 (one CPU, hours per run). Must be run as one factor of a 2x2 with candidate 3.

design_candidates.name: Axis-respecting positive views, inputs and matching
design_candidates.change: In reference_adapter.positive_views remove the horizontal flip of odd views, the +/-12 degree rotation, the 0.92-1.08 scale and the per-channel RGB gain/bias; keep +/-3 px time shifts, add time masking and frequency masking (SpecAugment style, masked region set to the row mean) and random frequency-band gain (FilterAugment style). Apply the same view set to synthetic training positives. Add one fixed input channel to PartEncoder.inputs that encodes the frequency row (a linear ramp, CoordConv/FAC style; 7 to 8 input channels). In the readout, compare descriptors only at matching frequency rows: no vertical translation search, and offer a frequency-row-profile pooling (pool over time only) as a readout option alongside the 6x6 grid. Treat the 96x96 letterbox of 140x170 crops as a loss of frequency resolution and test a taller input.
design_candidates.mechanism: Contrastive models become invariant to exactly their augmentations; rotation and vertical geometry make features invariant to frequency position, which is class identity for glitches (Blip 30-250 Hz, Power Line at 60 Hz harmonics, 1080 Lines, Whistle above 128 Hz). In the one controlled spectrogram-image study, vertical flips and color filters lowered PR AUC below no augmentation while time flips helped and time/frequency masking was neutral. Ordinary convolution wrongly enforces translation equivariance along frequency; adding a frequency-position input with 515 parameters matched an 8M-parameter method, and CoordConv lets a layer choose position dependence. The learned network is handicapped by these views in a way the random network is not, so removing them can only narrow the trained-minus-random gap.
design_candidates.expected_effect: Small to moderate on the readout side for both arms (frequency-row-profile pooling gave 0.546 vs 0.539 on DEV for the random middle block, unpublished DEV-only number) and a removal of a training handicap whose size is unknown. Line classes (Power_Line, 1080Lines) are the predicted winners; Chirp may lose. Not sufficient alone to make trained beat random.
design_candidates.cost: Very low: a few lines in reference_adapter and PartEncoder.inputs, one extra readout; no new data; re-scoring DEV takes minutes on one CPU. Applied to every arm of the 2x2.

design_candidates.name: Spectrogram-like synthetic distribution chosen by a label-free coverage diagnostic
design_candidates.change: Replace the flat, clean object-program drawings with a generator whose images are a colored-noise background (1/f^alpha with sampled alpha, plus stationary horizontal lines) carrying one to a few events drawn from primitives with spectrogram meaning: smooth Gaussian blobs (teardrops), chirped streaks (frequency sweeps), periodic horizontal bands, broadband vertical bursts, repeated event trains with sampled spacing, and arches; every primitive parameter (center frequency row, duration, bandwidth, chirp rate, SNR, repetition period) is sampled per member. Scale the number of families into the thousands; each family is a region of parameter space, not one program. Before any training run, score each candidate generator by a label-free diagnostic: recall/coverage of the 600 declared unlabeled spectrograms in random-CNN early-layer feature space (Baradad's recall measure) and intra-image self-similarity; pick the generator with the highest coverage. Run as the second factor of the 2x2 with candidate 1.
design_candidates.mechanism: Diversity (recall r=0.83) and natural color statistics (r=-0.57) predict transfer while flat-shape generators transfer worst and textured, oriented ones best (Squares 0.35, Shapes 0.39, Textures 0.41, Oriented 0.43); transfer grows log-linearly with the number of distinct programs and the worst programs collapse to repetitive shapes or solid color; category count matters more than instances; contour variety is crucial. The audio FDSL line shows that harmonic stacks, frequency modulation, envelopes, filtered noise and background noise pretrain a 1.1M-parameter CRNN from PSDS1 0.352 to 0.405 (Formula-SED, 2025), and the 2026 AudioPG ablation (unverified beyond arXiv HTML) places the biggest single jump at adding damping plus noise. Glitch types are blobs, streaks and lines in colored noise, so a generator of that kind gives the network statistics to keep rather than discard.
design_candidates.data_budget_change: none beyond the already-declared 600 unlabeled spectrograms, which are used only to score generators (no labels, no training on them)
design_candidates.expected_effect: Largest predicted effect of the synthetic-only options, but unquantified for this metric: all published gains are linear-probe transfer with thousands of labels. The diagnostic should rank generators without spending training runs; the 2x2 tells whether data or objective carried any gain.
design_candidates.cost: Moderate to high: a new 2D generator (several days), the diagnostic script (hours), and the same training cost per run as v0.14 on one CPU. Rendering 2D images needs no GPU.

design_candidates.name: Measurement prerequisites: per-arm normalization, multi-seed random control, fusion bar
design_candidates.change: Before any training: (1) freeze a per-arm normalization in protocol.json (per-image z for pixels, the 600-image per-feature standardizer for CNN readouts, each chosen on DEV and justified by the 15x row-wise standard-deviation spread); fix scripts/gravity_spy_v04.py so the raw-pixel control is not pushed through the per-feature standardizer (inferred from imports, verify first); (2) draw at least 5-10 random initializations of the same architecture and a width sweep (e.g. 0.5x, 1x, 2x channels) and report the control as mean and spread, so a trained block must clear the control's interval, not one seed; (3) add the label-free fusion arm (z-score sum of per-image-z raw pixels and the random early-layer mix; 0.597 DEV unpublished) and unwhitened PCA on the 600 images as named arms; (4) write a blank-image rule (139 constant-floor images; replace a blank frozen reference by the next non-blank one by rule, report with and without).
design_candidates.mechanism: This does not by itself make learned features beat random features; it makes the bar honest and measurable. Saxe averaged 10 random weight sets per architecture and Ramanujan 5 seeds with +/-1 SD; random networks differing only in seed share as little as 44% RDM variance in deep layers, so a single-seed control could sit anywhere in its own distribution and the -0.004 to -0.029 trained-minus-random differences cannot be interpreted without it. The normalization asymmetry currently penalizes pixels by 0.106 mAP and the fusion raises the bar every learned feature must clear.
design_candidates.expected_effect: Raises the reference bar on DEV from 0.582 (all-random four-layer mix) to about 0.597 (fusion, unpublished, no interval) and yields the first measured seed spread of the control; the width sweep may move the random bar up further (random-feature quality rises with width in Pons and Serra, Xue and Roshan, Ramanujan). Makes every later claim defensible to a reviewer.
design_candidates.cost: Lowest of all: re-scoring DEV with 10 random seeds is CPU minutes per seed; no training. Execute first even though it ranks fourth on effect.

design_candidates.name: Rank preservation: loss on backbone features, no projector, early readout kept
design_candidates.change: Apply the family-level objective (candidate 1) to a fixed subvector of the pooled coarse features (DirectCLR style) instead of through the 112*14 to 256 to 128 embedding MLP; keep the embedding MLP out of the loss or remove it. Keep the early-layer readouts (stem, fine, middle, coarse grids) as the declared retrieval features and log the singular-value spectrum of each block's pooled features at epoch 0, 1 and end of training, plus the per-layer DEV probe, as a tunnel detector. Prefer thousands of families and the native 140x170 aspect over 96x96.
design_candidates.mechanism: OOD probe performance tracks the numerical rank of deep representations and the tunnel that compresses them appears early in training; it is worst for low-diversity, few-class data and shrinks with many classes and higher resolution. Dimensional collapse is driven by strong augmentation and implicit low-rank regularization in over-parameterized projectors; removing the trainable projector outperforms SimCLR with a linear projector. HyperNet's trained global embedding is the worst readout of all (TEST 0.25-0.43), so the projector path is where the information is lost.
design_candidates.expected_effect: Expected to keep deep-block rank closer to the random start and therefore the coarse-block probe closer to or above its random control; the epoch-0 vs epoch-1 spectrum log will show whether it worked. No published number predicts the size on this metric.
design_candidates.cost: Low: a loss-path change and a logging script; same training cost. Confounded with candidate 1 unless run as a separate arm, so run it as an ablation on the winning 2x2 cell.

design_candidates.name: In-domain unlabeled pretraining as a declared separate budget
design_candidates.change: Build a pool of tens of thousands of O3 glitch spectrograms from Zenodo 5649212 (downloaded with gwpy GravitySpyTable.download, cropped and converted to one scalar), disjoint by gravityspy_id and time group from DEV, TEST v1.1 and the fresh O3 test set, hashed into protocol.json like the 600-image set. Train HyperNet's own CNN from random weights with a masked-reconstruction objective (unaugmented, CTSAE style, or low mask ratio) or a BYOL-A-style non-contrastive objective with only time shift, small frequency-band gain, additive noise and gain. Freeze, read early layers, and report this arm separately as 'in-domain unlabeled pretraining, N images' next to the synthetic-only arms; never include haystack or test items (if ever done, label it transductive and report both).
design_candidates.mechanism: This is the one lever the literature shows reliably closes the gap: BYOL-A trains a 600k-parameter CNN from scratch on spectrograms and loses only 1 point when the pool drops tenfold to 210k clips; an unaugmented autoencoder on 41,745 Gravity Spy O3 glitches beats the supervised DIRECT embedding on clustering (ARI 0.4091 vs 0.2137); masked/denoising pretraining is robust to small sets where joint-embedding methods degrade; in-domain SimCLR on 55k-178k radio cutouts beats ImageNet by more than 10 points. Real glitch statistics are the exact texture class the random network already partially captures, so a from-scratch model trained on them should keep and sharpen those features rather than discard them.
design_candidates.data_budget_change: Large and must be declared: adds roughly 10^4 to 10^5 unlabeled in-domain spectrograms as a separate pretraining budget; one labeled reference at enrollment is unchanged.
design_candidates.expected_effect: Highest documented effect of any option, but the 10^4-10^5 threshold is assembled from fine-tuning studies, not frozen one-shot readouts, and no 1-shot in-domain SSL result on scientific images exists. The v1.1 train split alone (a few thousand images) sits at the lower edge where SSL reliably helps.
design_candidates.cost: Highest: downloading tens of thousands of PNGs in small batches (hours to days), CPU training of a 755k-parameter CNN on 140x170 images (hours to a day per run), plus a leakage audit. Changes the project's stated data budget.

design_candidates.name: Physics injection families rendered through the Gravity Spy pipeline
design_candidates.change: Generate colored Gaussian noise from an analytic aLIGO PSD (pycbc.psd.aLIGOZeroDetHighPower plus pycbc.noise.noise_from_psd, seeded), inject parameterized families with published ranges (sine-Gaussians f0 40-1500 Hz, Q 2-20; Gaussian pulses; ring-downs; white-noise bursts; frequency-swept sine-Gaussians for whistles; scattered-light arches h = A sin[(f_harm/f_mod) sin 2 pi f_mod t]; narrow lines at 60 Hz harmonics and 1080 Hz; blip trains at 0.25-0.5 s; PyCBC chirps), render with gwpy q_transform under the Gravity Spy configuration (Q 4-64, 10-2048 Hz, whiten, 0.5/1/2/4 s windows, normalized energy 0-25.5) and read scalar energy directly. Each family is a parameter distribution; use it either as the candidate-3 generator or as a second data arm.
design_candidates.mechanism: These families are the literal definitions of the Gravity Spy classes (Blip teardrop, Tomte 16-150 Hz, Power Line at 60 Hz harmonics, Repeating Blips every 0.25-0.5 s, Scattered Light arches with f_mod about 1/6 Hz), and the rendering path is the archive's own, so the gap between training and test statistics is the smallest any synthetic generator can reach without real data. For noise-type priors, 1/f^alpha spectral noise is the best synthetic pretraining source (noise-INR, 2026, abstract only, unverified).
design_candidates.data_budget_change: none (no real strain or images; an analytic PSD and seeded noise only)
design_candidates.expected_effect: Unknown: no paper trains on injections and tests on real Gravity Spy images (Razzano and Cuoco 0.998 and Llorens-Monteagudo 96% test only on synthetic data), and the 2026 GlitchGAN paper (unverified) reports the Gravity Spy classifier accepting only about 79% of synthetic glitches. v0.4 would be the first measurement of this sim-to-real gap, which is itself a reportable result.
design_candidates.cost: High: a time-domain injection pipeline plus gwpy q_transform per image (about 0.2 s per sample reported, so 100k images is several CPU hours) and PSD validity checks; rendered images are not pixel-identical to archive PNGs, so DEV-side calibration of the scalar is needed.

fresh_data_plan: Source: Gravity Spy O3a/O3b rows from Zenodo 5649212 (CC BY 4.0; eight CSVs with event_time, peak_time, snr, gravityspy_id, 22 per-class confidences, ml_label, ml_confidence, url1-url4 for 0.5/1/2/4 s Omega scans) [https://zenodo.org/records/5649212]; Glanzer et al. report 233,981 H1 and 379,805 L1 glitches through O3b [https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12849]. Disjointness: v1.1 (Nov 2018, GPS 1127425468 to 1163924453) predates O3, so O3 rows cannot have been scored; confirm by matching gravityspy_id against the v1.1 metadata CSV (not yet done). Selection: ml_confidence >= 0.95 AND agreement with the retired volunteer consensus label in Zenodo 5911227 (min 2 classifications, >0.9 posterior) [https://zenodo.org/records/5911227]; cluster rows by event_time (a few seconds) before sampling and keep one event per cluster, with all four durations of one gravityspy_id in one group. Size: up to about 200 events per type per detector where available; Chirp (8 H1 + 12 L1 at p>0.9), Wandering Line (10 + 28) and Helix (15 + 37) cannot support per-class claims and are reported with wide intervals or dropped [https://arxiv.org/html/2208.12849v2]. Class map: O3 has 23 classes (adds Fast_Scattering and Blip_Low_Frequency, drops None_of_the_Above), so the 20-type list and the rare set are remapped in writing before download. Download: gwpy GravitySpyTable.download(download_durs=(0.5,1.0,2.0,4.0)) in small batches as the Zenodo page requests; no rate limit is documented [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gwpy/gwpy/main/gwpy/table/gravityspy.py]. Preprocessing: apply the v1.1 crop x=[66,532], y=[105,671] [https://zenodo.org/records/1486046], convert the viridis PNG to one scalar (the map to the h5 scalar is unverified; luma is a guess from the 0.0832 floor), declare the fresh set as a NEW protocol rather than a reproduction of the h5 arrays, and calibrate the scalar on DEV-equivalent O3 rows that are then excluded. References: draw the one reference per type from a separate O3 reference pool by a written rule (fixed random seed, non-blank), never from the test rows. Haystack: the remaining roughly 300k O3 rows with ML labels hidden serve the false-alarm estimate. Governance: write protocol.json (date, SHA-256, references, readouts, per-arm normalization, selection rule, bootstrap unit, class map) before scoring, score once, and report the old-vs-fresh gap as a result (new test sets move scores mainly by distribution shift, not adaptivity) [https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10811]. No O4 Gravity Spy image or label release exists on Zenodo; GWOSC O4a strain could build an unlabeled discovery haystack with self-rendered q-transforms but not a scored benchmark, and gwosc.org could not be fetched in this session.
false_alarm_plan: Restate the problem first: the 'about 90 per 10,000 for every method' figure is the 1% DEV cutoff by construction (100 per 10,000), and TEST v1.1 with about 1,100 negatives per target cannot certify any rate below roughly 25 per 10,000 (rule of three: 3/n), so a one-in-10,000 claim needs the O3 haystack from Zenodo 5649212 (roughly 300k rows with ML labels withheld; 100k negatives bound the rate at 0.3 per 10,000 with zero observed) and must be reported with a binomial interval and the negative count behind it. Then add label-free score corrections, each with its parameter chosen on DEV only and frozen in protocol.json before TEST: (1) adaptive cohort normalization of the reference-by-archive cosine matrix, z-scoring each score against the top-N most similar unlabeled archive items on both sides (about 20% relative EER/minDCF gain with an in-domain top-40 cohort in Thienpondt et al.; a mismatched cohort was worse than none, so the cohort must be the same archive) [https://arxiv.org/html/2007.07689v2]; (2) hubness correction by Mutual Proximity (skewness 2.5 to 0.29 across 30 datasets, no significant loss) [https://jmlr.org/papers/volume13/schnitzer12a/schnitzer12a.pdf] or k-reciprocal re-ranking, whose gain depends on several true matches per query (Market-1501 mAP 46.0 to 59.9, none on single-shot CUHK03) [https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1701.08398]; (3) fusion of the four durations (mean or product of normalized per-duration scores), which raised Gravity Spy accuracy from 92.9-95.3% single view to 96.9% merged and 0.911 to 0.941 with attention fusion [https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1705.00034], [https://arxiv.org/html/2401.12913v2]; (4) a per-reference tail threshold from a Generalized Pareto fit to the normalized impostor scores (SPOT, needs about 1,000 initial values, converges to the true quantile) [https://www.eecs.yorku.ca/course_archive/2018-19/F/6412/reading/kdd17p1067.pdf], replacing the single global 1% cutoff. Expect 20-40% relative reductions per method; no source documents a 10x reduction from normalization, hubness correction or test-time augmentation alone, and only cascades with a second independent verifier reach 100x [https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse576/21sp/notes/11_FaceDetRec_21.pdf]; HyperNet has no second verifier today, so a 10x claim should not be made in v0.4. Report TEST and fresh-set false alarms per 10,000 at the DEV-chosen cutoff with a 95% binomial interval, recall at that cutoff per type, and the number of negatives behind the operating point. CSLS and AS-norm numbers from Conneau and Matejka were not fully verified in this pass and are not relied on.
evaluation_changes: Measure the random control's seed-to-seed spread: at least 5-10 random initializations of the same architecture (Saxe averaged 10 sets on NORB and 5 on CIFAR-10; Ramanujan used 5 seeds with +/-1 SD) plus a width sweep, and require a trained block to clear the control's interval, not one seed-1403 draw.

Freeze normalization per arm in protocol.json before scoring (per-image z for pixels, the 600-image standardizer for CNN readouts, each chosen on DEV), and verify that scripts/gravity_spy_v04.py does not pass the raw-pixel control through the per-feature standardizer (currently inferred, not verified).

Run the v0.4 training changes as a 2x2 factorial (old data/new objective, new data/old objective, both, neither) with identical seeds, so any gain can be attributed to the objective or the generator; add candidate 5 as an ablation on the winning cell.

Add a label-free pre-training generator diagnostic: recall/coverage of the 600 declared unlabeled spectrograms in random-CNN early-layer feature space and intra-image self-similarity, scored before any training run.

Report paired differences at event level and class level with cluster bootstrap over time groups (events within a few seconds of a reference or of each other) and over the four durations of one gravityspy_id; state the number of such groups in TEST and the fresh set.

Report mean AP together with recall at a stated false-alarm count, with the count of negatives that set the operating point and the rule-of-three ceiling (TEST v1.1: about 25 per 10,000); never ROC alone (Saito and Rehmsmeier).

Keep named fixed-extractor arms with paired differences: raw pixels (per-image z), unwhitened PCA on the 600 images, the label-free fusion of pixels and the random early mix, HOG, and Kymatio Scattering2D on the 140x170 image (no rotation averaging); cite the absence of a runnable DIRECT/OmegaNeuron baseline.

Score each candidate as the fusion (mean or product of normalized scores) over the 0.5/1/2/4 s views as an additional readout, since the durations are views of the same event and fusion is free in the one-reference protocol.
Write a blank-image rule in protocol.json (139 constant-floor 1.0 s images, two blank frozen references) and report results with and without blanks.

Document every past use of TEST v1.1 (v0.1, v0.2, v0.3, the v15 draw of 4,044 previously unexposed rows) and what was selected on it; make the fresh O3 set the single confirmatory run, with protocol.json hashed and dated before scoring, and report the old-vs-fresh gap as a result.
State the minimum detectable paired effect (roughly 0.015-0.045 mAP from v0.3 interval widths, an unpublished back-calculation) so that differences inside it are reported as ties.

Flag every 2025-2026 source (Licciardi WST, Formula-SED, AudioPG, FormulaBank, noise-INR, OmegaNeuron, Cirfeta, Wu et al. revisions) as read from arXiv HTML only until the PDFs or journal versions are checked.

Score normalization and hubness gains to expect for false alarms: adaptive s-norm top-40 in-domain cohort EER 2.14% to 1.69%, minDCF 0.0947 to 0.0759 [https://arxiv.org/html/2007.07689v2]; Mutual Proximity hub skewness 2.5 to 0.29 [https://jmlr.org/papers/volume13/schnitzer12a/schnitzer12a.pdf]; k-reciprocal re-ranking Market-1501 mAP 46.00 to 59.87 [https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1701.08398]; OpenMax +4.3% F-measure over best SoftMax threshold [https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1511.06233]

missing_questions.prompt: Research a synthetic data family nobody in the nine threads considered: physics-parameterized glitch surrogates rendered through Gravity Spy's OWN Q-transform pipeline instead of 2D drawings. The Gravity Spy repo (develop branch, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gravity-Spy/GravitySpy/develop/gravityspy/utils/utils.py and .../gravityspy/plot/plot.py) fixes the rendering: 16384 Hz, 64 s block, q_transform(qrange=(4,64), frange=(10,2048), whiten=True, fres=0.5, tres=0.002, search=0.5), plot windows 0.5/1/2/4 s, log2 frequency axis, viridis, clim (0, 25.5), figsize [8,6]. (1) Catalogue the standard burst-search waveform families and their parameter ranges as used by cWB, BayesWave, oLIB, Powell et al. 2015/2017 (simulated glitch classification: sine-Gaussians, Gaussians, ring-downs, chirps, whistles), Razzano & Cuoco 2018, the 2018 dictionary-learning paper (arXiv 1811.03867, glitches injected into aLIGO-PSD-weighted Gaussian noise), arXiv 2308.08429 (sine-Gaussian 40-300 Hz injections) and SiGMa-Net II (arXiv 2601.17882): sine-Gaussian (f0, Q, amplitude, phase), chirplet/linear chirp, Gaussian pulse, white-noise burst, ring-down, scattered-light arches (f(t)=2 v_mirror/lambda |sin|), stationary lines/combs with wandering, repeating-blip trains. weak_spots: Spectrogram-specific thread's colormap-decoding recommendation assumes RGB colormap input, but the v0.1-v0.3 benchmark feeds a single scalar from trainingsetv1d1.h5 replicated to three channels (hypernet/gravity_spy.py to_uint8_rgb), so the per-channel RGB gain in reference_adapter acts only as a brightness gain and 'decode viridis' reduces to inverting a monotone 1-D curve. The blank-image floor 0.0832 is close to the Rec.709 luma of viridis' darkest color (about 0.084), which suggests the h5 scalar is luma of the viridis PNG, but this is my inference, not a verified fact; the 2026 DINOv2 'hue carries detector information' claim does not apply to the h5 benchmark.

'TEST v1.1 has been used three times' understates exposure: the v15 experiment drew its 4,044 'fresh' events from previously unexposed v1.1 events (its README excludes prior exposed time groups before acquisition), so essentially all of v1.1, including the train split, has been scored under some protocol. Fresh data means O3 (Zenodo 5649212), where Chirp (20 at p>0.9) and Wandering Line (38) cannot support per-class claims.

The v0.3 verdict that a trained block never beats the same block at random rests on one random start (seed 1403) and one training seed per curriculum; differences of -0.004 to -0.029 mAP are plausibly within seed-to-seed variance of the random control, which was never measured.

The 'about 90 false alarms per 10,000 for every method' figure is a consequence of the chosen 1% DEV cutoff (100 per 10,000 by construction), not a measured property of the methods; open problem (3) is partly a framing artifact, and TEST v1.1 (1,179 items, about 1,100 negatives per target) cannot certify any rate below roughly 25 per 10,000 (rule of three).

Raw pixels with the 600-image per-feature standardization score 0.379 vs 0.485 unscaled; the same standardization is applied to all CNN readouts, so every CNN-vs-pixels comparison and the 0.576 random-mix number depend on an unexamined normalization choice that demonstrably hurts at least one arm.

Synthetic-pretraining thread's statement that 'every synthetic pretraining beats random init by a large margin' comes from linear-probe or fine-tuning transfer with thousands of real labels on natural images (Baradad 2021/2022, FractalDB, VisualAtom); none measures frozen cosine one-reference retrieval, so it does not predict HyperNet's metric, and the Baradad random-CNN figures (0.21 AlexNet Table 2 vs 10.84% MoCo/ResNet) come from different backbones and tables and should not be mixed.

WST 88.57% (2411.19122), Formula-SED (2504.04428), AudioPG (2606.14791), FormulaBank (2609.15067), noise-INR (2603.29034), Cirfeta DINOv2 (2605.28572), Wu et al. Coughlin et al. 2019's Water Jet raw-pixel result is internally inconsistent in the ar5iv rendering (30.0% rejection at 50% retention in text vs 99.0% in the Figure 3 caption); the prior-work thread's claim that learned embeddings only win on subtle classes rests on this unresolved number.

In-domain SSL thread's 10^4-10^5-image threshold is assembled from fine-tuning studies (Ciga, Cao & Wu, BYOL-A), not frozen one-shot readouts, and the CTSAE-beats-DIRECT comparison is on O3 data where DIRECT was trained on O1 classes, so it conflates domain shift with the label-free advantage.

Gravity Spy Q-scan parameters (qrange 4-64, frange 10-2048, whiten=True, fres 0.5, tres 0.002, log2 frequency axis, viridis, clim 0-25.5, figsize [8,6]) were read from the repo's develop branch in this session; the DPI / 800x600 output and the strain channel and frametype are not defaulted in code, so regenerated images from GWOSC will not be pixel-identical to the archive PNGs. The objectives thread's primary fix (family-member positives plus SupCon/classification) and the synthetic thread's data fix (1/f backgrounds, blobs, chirps) are proposed jointly; no thread designed the 2x2 factorial (old data/new objective, new data/old objective) needed to attribute any v0.4 gain, and none proposed a label-free pre-training diagnostic (e.g., Baradad-style recall/coverage of the synthetic set measured in random-CNN feature space against the 600 unlabeled spectrograms) to pick a generator before spending training runs.
